note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent auditor) after the user-namespace conversion (25fbb6e890/d8427e4380): the TestVRRPRedirectSourceFollowsVirtualMAC unit gained only `if !userns.Enter(t) { return }` as its first statement and its build tag moved from integration&&linux to linux. userns.Enter (internal/test/userns/userns_linux.go) re-runs the one named test in a fresh user+net+mount namespace and returns false to the parent only when the child reported PASS or SKIP; a failing child, a non-zero exit, or a child that ran nothing calls t.Fatalf, so every assertion below the guard still fails the test when the behaviour breaks. Body otherwise byte-identical. RFC 3768 Section 8.1: "If a VRRP router is acting as Master for virtual router(s) containing addresses it does not own, then it must determine which virtual router the packet was sent to when selecting the redirect source address." Fresh judgement: two non-owner groups on one LAN, reverse route pinned through the parent with source .254; a frame to each virtual MAC must draw a redirect sourced from that group's own VIP, and a frame to the physical MAC from .254, so a route-picked or wrong-group source fails. Enforced.
